title: When solar panels retire: can they be recycled?
description: A solar panel works for roughly 25 to 30 years. As the first big generations of panels reach retirement, a new question matters for your wallet and the planet: what happens to them next?

body.heading: Mostly glass, metal — and value
paragraphs: A typical panel is mostly glass and an aluminium frame, with silicon cells and small amounts of silver and copper inside. Those materials are worth recovering: specialist recyclers can reclaim the great majority of a panel's mass, and the metals go straight back into manufacturing.
The catch is cost and scale. Recycling a panel still costs more than sending it to landfill in many places, which is why rules and take-back schemes are only now catching up with the retirement wave.

body.heading: What it means when you buy
paragraphs: When you get quotes, ask what the installer does with old panels and whether the manufacturer runs a take-back programme. A slightly higher quote that includes end-of-life handling can be the cheaper honest price over the panel's whole life.
And a retiring panel is not always a dead one: panels that have lost some output can still serve in lower-demand roles, so reuse comes before recycling in the waste hierarchy.

takeaway: Retired solar panels are mostly recyclable glass and metal — ask installers about take-back schemes, because landfill is the lazy option, not the only one.
